manuscript_destination: Method: Notation and reference layer; Factorizing the patch computation; Output calculation and implementation; Experimental design: Agreement checks

claim: The repaired numerical contract passes every registered smooth and N088 check and every structured F row; 33 finite T/FP32 small-U-Net rows miss the registered aggregate tolerance.

claim: The F path is faster than R in forward and forward-plus-backward execution for all three corrected convolution anchors; block and dense-stack gains are smaller or uncertain.

claim: All fifteen CIFAR-100 R/F/T runs completed; F training compute is faster than R, while the positive fixed-final F-R accuracy point estimate is descriptive rather than an accuracy contribution.

claim: Primary systems timing, memory, profile, and scaling evidence comes from one V100/CUDA-11.8 platform; training evidence comprises separate original V100 and prospective A6000 cohorts, with post-hoc complete-model A6000 controls, a current-JAX check, and a PyTorch/HypLL cross-check reported separately.

claim: Across the complete-U-Net update scaling sweep, F was faster and used less process-lifetime peak live allocation than R at every workload where both paths completed; at batch 8 and 512 x 512, all five F sessions completed while all five R sessions ended in recorded first-update allocator OOMs.
scope: Seven registered workloads spanning batch sizes 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16 at 256 x 256 and resolutions 128, 256, and 512 at batch 8; five fresh-process sessions per path on one V100 with 32 GiB physical memory under CUDA 11.8 and a captured 23.81-GiB JAX allocator limit.
caveat: The 512 x 512 speedup is not estimable because R did not complete; the failure diagnostic reports a 23.01-GiB compiled allocation under the captured allocator limit, not exhaustion of all physical memory; peak live allocation includes initialization, compilation, and warmup and is not isolated activation memory; capacity and timing are allocator-, platform-, and implementation-specific.
manuscript_destination: Results: Complete U-Net runtime and memory (Figure 2); Appendix: Additional comparisons (Scaling estimates)

claim: A same-machine clean-clone technical preflight reproduced the bounded E02 acceptance gate and the direction of the batch-eight complete-U-Net update gain: 424 numerical rows with 40/40 required same-precision groups, and paired R/F speedup 1.745 [1.557, 1.956].

caveat: M/F is a bundled execution contrast and is not a pure cuDNN estimate; this post-hoc A6000 cohort is not pooled with V100 results.

claim: Building R's patch by gathering shifted slices (Rg) makes the reference 1.138 [1.134, 1.142] times faster for the U-Net update and 1.047 [1.035, 1.060] for the ResNet-20 update; F remains 1.819 [1.807, 1.831] and 1.637 [1.569, 1.708] times faster than Rg and uses 47% less peak memory for the U-Net update. Removing the ball mapping from Rg's patch (Mg) gives 1.445 [1.434, 1.457] of the U-Net gain and native convolution of the patch statistics a further 1.258 [1.241, 1.276].
scope: Paired randomized fresh-process R/Rg/Mg/F sessions, five per workload, on the RTX A6000 with JAX 0.4.25 and CUDA 11.8 at three U-Net boundaries and the ResNet-20 batch-128 update.
caveat: Post-hoc control. The R/Mg contrast is reported in addition to the five registered contrasts. Mg/F bundles materialization, contraction, and backend selection. Compiled buffer-assignment bytes are zero in this run and are not reported. Not pooled with E24/E25.
manuscript_destination: Results: Speedup attribution and Euclidean reference (Table 5)

claim: A factorized PyTorch replacement for HypLL 0.1.1 HConvolution2d reproduces the official layer's outputs and gradients to a relative L2 error of at most 1.0e-14 in FP64 and 4.3e-6 in FP32, accelerates S1-S3 forward-plus-gradient calls 1.43, 6.26, and 11.7 times with 3.9 to 9.0 times lower steady-state peak allocation, and makes a complete Hyperbolic U-Net training step 1.41 [1.41, 1.42] times faster with peak memory reduced from 13.6 to 6.8 GiB.
scope: RTX A6000 with PyTorch 2.4.0 (CUDA 12.1), HypLL 0.1.1, and the upstream Hyperbolic U-Net at bec504e2f4d1; five fresh-process paired sessions per workload; 40 FP64 and 40 FP32 agreement comparisons on S1-S3 and a stride-2 case.
caveat: Post-hoc and not registered in protocol.yaml. Steady-state peaks exclude setup and warmup. The upstream U-Net uses iterative Frechet batch normalization rather than the paper's midpoint normalization. Results are specific to this PyTorch/HypLL version.
manuscript_destination: Results: Official HypLL implementation; Supplementary Table S12

claim: On CPU (TFRT_CPU_0), against an FP64 oracle that keeps the FP32 projection margin, F and R have the same FP32 accuracy: the median per-tensor ratio of F's to R's relative L2 error is 0.97 to 1.01 for outputs and gradients at curvatures 0.06, 0.1, and 0.13. Negating the single pre-ReLU element closest to zero in small-U-Net realization 2 changes the gradients by the magnitudes recorded in E02/E26, whereas shifting the radius cap by up to two units in the last place changes no decision. The source-radius cap is active in at most 2.6e-8 of evaluated patches in the final E09/E10 checkpoints.
scope: CPU (TFRT_CPU_0) runs with JAX 0.4.25: ten FP32 realizations per structured case at three curvatures for the oracle comparison, small-U-Net realization 2 for the branch trace, and the official-test batches of all final E09/E10 R/F checkpoints for cap activity.
caveat: Post-hoc and not registered in protocol.yaml. The oracle evaluates the same clipped function in FP64, so it measures FP32 rounding error, not error against unclipped real arithmetic.
manuscript_destination: Results: Agreement with the reference (Table 2); Supplementary Table S11

claim: At the three retained seed-11 ResNet-20 states of E07-J2, F's FP32 gradients are closer than R's to an FP64 oracle: whole-gradient relative L2 errors are 0.009, 0.023, and 0.040 for F and 0.056, 0.045, and 0.074 for R, and T matches F within 1e-4. The recomputed F-R differences (0.054, 0.067, 0.113) reproduce E07-J2.
scope: Final-update E10 seed-11 R, F, and T checkpoints and the E07-J2 batch; FP32 on the E07-J2 V100 with JAX 0.4.25 and CUDA 11.8; oracle R in FP64 with the FP32 projection margin on the same GPU.
caveat: Post-hoc (protocol 1.20). One seed and one batch; the largest error of every path is in the stem-convolution weight gradient. FP32 logits matched E07-J2 bitwise in 4 of 9 cases, so convolution-algorithm selection can differ between processes.
manuscript_destination: Appendix C.3 (Table 11); Discussion
